title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from pages 9–10). Grothendieck is trying to build a 'Galois–Teichmüller category'. Its objects are algebraic curves of type (g,ν), meaning genus g with ν punctures. Its arrows include finite covering morphisms X→Y and not only isomorphisms, so it is a category and not a groupoid. The goal is for it to be, over C, a kind of profinite completion of a topological 'isotopy category' of surface maps. On page 9 he finds an obstacle. A general map between punctured surfaces has no canonical factorisation, up to isotopy, as an inclusion of the 'hole-filling' type followed by a finite covering Y'→Y that is ramified only over points of Y. So he cannot interpret his classes, or their profinite completions, through abstract topological groups when X and Y are complex curves (first lines of this page).

This page. He notes that over any algebraically closed field k one should at least have a functor of the following kind.
- Source: the Teichmüller groupoid of curves of type (g,ν), together with a subset I of the marked points with |I| = ν' ≤ ν.
- Target: the Teichmüller groupoid of type (g, ν−ν').
- Operation: 'filling the holes' indexed by I.
- Compatibility: a transitivity property, so that filling holes all at once agrees with filling them in successive steps.

In modern terms, these are the point-forgetting (erasing) morphisms M_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν−ν'}. They induce maps on the algebraic, profinite fundamental groupoids based at tangential base points, which are the étale analogue of the Birman forgetful maps Γ_{g,ν} → Γ_{g,ν−ν'}. The transitivity condition is functoriality for the composite I ⊂ J.

The real difficulty is different. He wants a notion of 'inclusion morphisms', which are open immersions of a punctured curve into a curve with fewer punctures. These would have to compose with the covering morphisms already present in the Galois–Teichmüller category. He sees no natural way to do this. Page 10 continues: one could brute-force a bigger category by generators and relations. But then, over C, it becomes problematic to identify the result with the profinite completion of the topological isotopy category.

So the page records an obstruction to merging two kinds of arrow into one profinite 'Teichmüller–Galois' category. One kind is étale coverings, where Galois actions on fundamental groups live. The other is hole-filling inclusions, the erasing maps of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical error. The proposal is heuristic and the difficulty he flags is genuine. Open immersions induce surjections on π1, not injections, and they do not lift canonically along coverings. Composites 'cover after inclusion' are therefore not canonically factorisable. This is the same non-factorisation issue noted on page 9.

ideas.what: Functor between Teichmüller groupoids of type (g,ν) and (g,ν−ν') given by filling the holes indexed by a subset I, with transitivity for successive fillings, defined over any algebraically closed field.
ideas.modern_name: Point-erasing / forgetful morphisms in the Teichmüller tower; Birman forgetful homomorphisms on (profinite) mapping class groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman (topological forgetful maps, 1969); in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller tower setting: Grothendieck's Esquisse, then Ihara, Drinfeld, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and its basic operations; whether hole-filling is explicitly listed there: unsure

ideas.what: Desire for a single 'Galois–Teichmüller category' whose arrows include both finite coverings and hole-filling inclusions, possibly defined by generators and relations.
ideas.modern_name: A profinite category of hyperbolic curves with étale maps and open immersions (compare Hom-form anabelian categories; profinite mapping class groupoids with coverings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard single source; related to the anabelian framework (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki) and to profinite Teichmüller theory (Boggi)

ideas.what: Concern (page 10) that the Galois–Teichmüller category over C should be the profinite completion of the topological isotopy category.
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups / 'goodness' of the profinite completion of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Asada, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki and others (genus 0, 1, 2 results); open in general
ideas.where_published: Esquisse touches on the profinite Teichmüller tower; the congruence issue is not explicitly formulated there as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly identifies the obstruction to building one category containing both covering morphisms and hole-filling inclusions of punctured curves, compatibly with a profinite-completion interpretation over C. He leaves it open, apart from a brute-force generators-and-relations option.
missed.quote: Mais je vois malaisément l'inclusion dans un notion correspondante de "morphismes d'inclusions", qui pourrait se composer avec les morphismes dont on dispose déjà dans la catégorie (pas groupoïde!) de Galois-Teichmüller.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Later work on the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group mainly uses the tower of moduli groupoids with erasing and gluing maps, or covering-type (Belyi) data, rarely both in one category. A unified 'covers + open immersions' profinite category with a congruence-type comparison would connect GT-theory with anabelian Hom-conjectures and with the congruence subgroup problem. This is a modest but explicit open design problem.

deep.surprise_reason: The forgetful functors are standard in the Teichmüller tower literature. The interesting part is the explicit recognition that coverings and inclusions do not combine naturally in a profinite Galois–Teichmüller category. That is an exploratory remark, close to known concerns such as the congruence subgroup problem, and not a result.
transcription_corrections: '[?] correspondant à des "morphismes d'inclusions"' should probably read 'notion correspondante de "morphismes d'inclusions"'.

'avec une partie [?] [-d-] I de cardinal [?] ν' ≤ ν [?] de points [?] impliqués [?] par I': the words after I are poorly legible; the sense is a subset I of the marked points with |I| = ν' ≤ ν, the points indexed by I.
'trous incidents [?]': uncertain reading; the sense is compatibility of a single filling with successive fillings.
'il [-doit être-] {+serait+} possible': the interlinear correction looks like 'serait'/'semble' with 'doit être' struck out; the reading is plausible.
